I'm reconstructing the timeline of the incident: the admin switched on the monthly-spend flag at 09:02, the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py started at that same time, and Argus turned the flag off at 09:07:20, yet the service stayed at incident level. I'm now checking the logs, which show the flag still evaluating as on at 09:09 and 09:12.

Now I'm matching the error timestamps against the flag evaluations: errors line up with the "on" evaluations at 09:09, 09:12 and 09:18–09:19, and the "off" ones are clean. The flag provider history shows Argus switched it off at 09:07:20 and nothing re-enabled it until 09:19:01, yet the service still evaluated "on" at several points, so the revert apparently didn't fully reach it.

The evaluation counts at 09:19 and the 09:02 and 09:07 splits look like partial rollouts within those minutes rather than a clean on or off. After the revert at 09:07:20, the service alternates between off and on evaluations while the provider stays off, so something is still serving the flag as on, likely a cache or a stale source, though I don't know which yet.

I'm weighing whether the service's own evaluations of the flag could be the cause, since the provider history shows it off from 09:07:20 to 09:19:01. I want to find out which source the service was reading when it kept evaluating the flag as on.

I'm weighing whether to turn the flag off again, since the revert was judged refuted and the errors track the flag's "on" evaluations exactly at 09:09, 09:12 and 09:18–09:19. I'd want to confirm at the service that every evaluation reads off and that the ZeroDivisionError lines stop and the error rate falls back toward baseline.

I'm tracing how the ZeroDivisionError lines up with the flag's on evaluations at 09:09, 09:12 and 09:18–09:19, and I'm starting to sketch the causal chain, beginning with what shoppers saw: account page requests failing.

I'm working through the causal chain now: shoppers' account page requests were failing, and those requests were raising a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py:47 starting at 09:02, which had not appeared in the logs before then. The errors line up with the service evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on, so requests were going down the new path. The one thing I haven't yet traced is why the flag was turned on at 09:02, since the admin switch is the step I'm checking against the deploy history.

I'm checking which other flags changed in that hour, and the provider history shows no other changes, so the earlier suspects are ruled out. Deploys are the remaining candidate, and I'm verifying the change events for that.

I'm checking whether any deploy happened in the day before the onset, since the change events read so far show none and all three replicas are on a single revision at 09:07:14.

I'm checking whether a deploy could be the cause: the change events for the day before the onset came back empty, and all three replicas were on one revision at 09:07:14, so no deploy stands out.

I'm settling on the root cause now: the new path divides a shopper's this-month total by the number of purchases made this month, so a shopper who bought before but not this month hits a zero divisor. The stack trace at line 47 fits division by zero, though the logs don't yet confirm that this specific condition is what triggers it.

I'm laying out the causal chain step by step now: first the shoppers' account pages failing, then the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 beginning at 09:02, with none in the logs before that. Next I'm tying those failures to the requests where the flag evaluated on, minute by minute.

I'm laying out the causal chain now: the shoppers' account pages were failing, and from 09:02 those requests raised a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, which hadn't appeared in the logs before. I'm also checking that the flag was evaluating on during exactly those minutes, and that the admin's switch at 09:02 is the step that brought it on.

I'm working out the contributing factors now: the check that would have caught the zero-divisor case before rollout was never run, and the flag went to all traffic at once rather than in stages.

I'm adding a contributing factor that nobody was paged, since the alert fired but no on-call incident was linked to it, and I'm pairing it with a fix to link the error-rate alert to on-call paging. I'm also starting to consider whether the alert's 10-minute averaging window delayed detection, though I haven't settled that yet.

I'm now looking at the contributing factors: the missing pre-enable check and the all-at-once flag rollout are already captured, and I'm noting that nobody was paged as its own finding. I'm also weighing whether the flag's evaluation drifting from the provider's state belongs among them, though it reads more like a question about the response than a cause, so I'm leaving it out of the factors and setting it aside. Next I'm starting on the action items, beginning with a prevention item for flag changes.

I'm drafting the action items now, with one prevention item for pre-enable testing of flags and another for staged rollout, plus a detection item to page the on-call when the error-rate alert fires. Then I'll move on to the lessons, starting with what went well: the investigator named the flag change.

I'm going through the lessons section now, starting with what went well: the Investigator Agent named the flag change and the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 as the candidate cause at T13. I'm also noting that Argus checked the flag provider history before acting at T15, and that the Investigator Agent matched errors to flag evaluations minute by minute on its second pass at T32.

I'm drafting the went-well list now, adding that the Investigator Agent tied the errors to the minutes the flag evaluated on when it looked again at T32, and that Code-Fix proposed a draft fix with tests in PR #419 at T36. Then I'm turning to the went-wrong list, where the Mitigation Agent judged the revert by the service's overall level and put the flag back on, even though the logs show the flag still evaluating on in some minutes after the revert.

I'm drafting the went-wrong list now: the Mitigation Agent judged the flag revert by the service's overall level alone and put the flag back on, which returned the service to evaluating it on for most requests. Then I'm noting that Argus moved to fixing while the harm was still ongoing, and that the second investigation's candidate C2, which tied the errors to the flag's evaluations minute by minute, was never acted on.

I'm drafting the got-lucky entry now: the revert didn't reach every evaluation, but the flag still evaluated off in most minutes before the put-back, and no ZeroDivisionError was logged in those minutes, which kept the harm down by chance. Then I'm turning to what's still at risk: account pages could keep failing for shoppers on the monthly spend path while the flag is back on.

I'm checking the symptom wording: account pages failed for shoppers, which is plain enough. For the plain-language cause, an administrator switched on a new account-page feature, and its code fails with a division by zero, most likely when it works out an average for a shopper who hasn't bought anything yet this month.

I'm settling on the root cause now: with the monthly-spend feature on, the account page takes the monthly-summary branch, where the per-item average divides by a count of this month's purchases. For a shopper who bought earlier but nothing this month, that count is zero, so the division at spend_summary.py fails and the request dies.

I'm settling the wording of the root cause now, keeping the exact count out of the prose and naming the error plainly. I'll describe the failing line in words rather than figures, and phrase the plain-language cause as the code dividing by the number of purchases a shopper made this month, which breaks for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

I'm checking the list of cases where the flag was still evaluating on after the revert, so I can figure out why the revert didn't reach every evaluation. I'm also noting that the provider history showed no change between the revert and the put-back, so the question is where the service reads the flag from.

I'm working out the stop-the-harm step now: switching the flag back off and confirming, in the service's logs, that every evaluation reads off and that the error rate drops back down.

I'm checking which minutes the errors fell in against when the flag evaluated on, since the ZeroDivisionError should appear only in those minutes. I'm writing the step that confirms this in the logs, with each figure kept in its own row so nothing gets mixed up.

I'm ruling out other flag changes next: the provider history shows no flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before this one, so this is the only change to check. I'm also noting that no deploy came back in the same window, since the earlier read-backs only turned up the one production change.

I'm checking whether "ruled out" holds for a deploy, since the change events for the day before the onset show nothing but this flag change, so I'll note that no deploy turns up in that window and that the replicas all sit on a single revision.

I'm checking the went-well list against the record: Argus read the flag provider's history before acting, and the history showed only the admin's switch.

I'm checking the step-1 wording now: shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors, which I can state without any figures and cite to the error-rate and incident records.

action_items.item: Before any io-shop feature flag is switched on in production, run the service's tests with that flag on, including accounts with no activity in the period the new path summarises.
Switch io-shop feature flags on in production by a growing share of requests rather than for all requests at once.
Link the ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop to the service's on-call paging, so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, logged in the minutes {G5309.3}. None of these lines were in the logs read from before then.

The failing requests were the ones on which monthly-spend-feature evaluated on. The flag evaluated off every minute over {G7e5d.4}, with no ZeroDivisionError, and evaluated on from {Gce95.4}. After the revert, the ZeroDivisionError lines at {G5309.7}, {G5309.8} and {G5309.9} fall in the minutes the flag evaluated on ({Gce95.8}, {Gce95.9}, {Gce95.10}, and {G971b.15} once it was put back on). None were logged in the minutes it evaluated off ({G7e5d.8}, {G7e5d.9}, {G7e5d.10}).

ruled_out.what: Another flag change: besides this switch-on, the flag provider's history showed no flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before each read.
A deploy: the change events read for the day before the onset held none, only this flag change, and all replicas ran a single revision when it was read.

causal_chain.step: The flag was evaluating on because admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}.
The code path the flag turns on divides by a count that can be empty, at the line named in the error.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched on a new feature for shoppers' account pages, and the code it turned on fails when it divides by a shopper's purchases this month, likely for shoppers who have bought before but nothing yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that ran the monthly-spend-feature code path, against an account with earlier purchases but none this month, before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The ZeroDivisionError would have shown up before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag was switched on for nearly every request at once: the service logged it on for most evaluations in the minute it changed and for all of them from the next minute.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout would have exposed only a small share of account page requests while the error rate rose, so far fewer shoppers would have hit the failure before the flag was stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been brought in when the alert fired, able to act on the flag while the automated revert was not holding.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

got_lucky: After the revert the flag evaluated off in most minutes before it was put back. No ZeroDivisionError was logged in those minutes, which held down the failures over that stretch.

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent named the switch-on of monthly-spend-feature and the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py as the leading candidate.
Argus read the flag provider's history before acting. Apart from this switch-on, it showed no flag change by anyone but Argus.
The Investigator Agent, investigating again, tied the errors to the minutes in which the flag evaluated on.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix, with tests, as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent judged the revert by the service's overall level alone. The service's own logs showed the flag still evaluating on in some minutes after the revert, and errors only in those minutes. Judging the revert refuted put the flag back on, and the flag then evaluated on for most requests again.
C2 tied the errors to the flag's evaluations minute by minute, but it was counted as already tested under C1, so nothing was done on it and the flag was left on when the incident moved to fixing.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` takes its `use_monthly_summary` branch, where `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month that number is {F1.1}, so line {F1.2} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature switched back on, account page requests that evaluate it on could keep failing with the same ZeroDivisionError.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Then confirm at io-shop that every minute's flag evaluations log monthly-spend-feature=off, that the ZeroDivisionError lines from src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stop, and that the account page error rate falls back toward {errors_before}.
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out where io-shop reads monthly-spend-feature from, and why it evaluated the flag on at {Gce95.8}, {Gce95.9} and {Gce95.10} after the revert at {P2.1}. Over that stretch the flag provider's history showed no change by anyone but Argus, and the service evaluated the flag off in the minutes between.
